holidays.name: International Body Piercing Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the art, culture, and self-expression of body piercing, from classic earlobe studs to elaborate adornments. Piercing studios and fans mark it by showing off their favorite jewelry.
holidays.origin: The day is an unofficial observance in the body modification community, reportedly started by piercing enthusiasts to recognize piercing as a form of personal expression and an ancient practice.
holidays.funFact: Ötzi the Iceman, a mummy about 5,300 years old, had stretched pierced earlobes, which shows that piercing is among the oldest known forms of body adornment.

holidays.name: Tau Day
holidays.description: A celebration of tau (τ), the circle constant equal to 2π, or about 6.28. Fans of math argue that tau makes circle math simpler and more intuitive than pi does. Many celebrate by eating pies, double the usual number.
holidays.origin: Physicist Michael Hartl launched the Tau Manifesto in 2010, arguing that tau, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its radius, is the more natural constant. The date 6/28 matches tau's first digits, 6.28.
holidays.funFact: Because tau is twice pi, Tau Day fans joke that you should eat twice as much pie, and some say a full circle's worth of pie is the proper way to celebrate.

holidays.name: Insurance Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to reminding people to review their insurance policies, from health and home to car and life. Not exactly a party, but surprisingly useful for avoiding future disasters.
holidays.origin: Insurance Awareness Day is observed annually on June 28 in the United States, promoted by insurance organizations to encourage people to understand their coverage and be prepared for the unexpected.
holidays.funFact: The modern insurance industry has roots in 17th-century London, where merchants gathered at Edward Lloyd's coffee house to underwrite ships' voyages, leading to the creation of Lloyd's of London.

holidays.name: Paul Bunyan Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the giant lumberjack of American folklore, his blue ox Babe, and tall tales of epic proportions. People celebrate with tall-tale storytelling, flapjack breakfasts, and flannel shirts.
holidays.origin: Paul Bunyan Day honors the legendary logger whose stories grew out of lumber camps and were popularized in early 20th-century advertising by the Red River Lumber Company, which published illustrated Bunyan stories.
holidays.funFact: According to legend, the Grand Canyon was carved when Paul Bunyan dragged his giant axe behind him, and Minnesota's 10,000 lakes were formed by Babe the Blue Ox's footprints filling with water.

holidays.name: National Logistics Day
holidays.description: A salute to the unseen workers and systems that make sure packages, groceries, and nearly everything else get where they are going. Celebrate by thanking a truck driver, warehouse worker, or the person who delivered your latest online order.
holidays.origin: The observance grew out of industry efforts to recognize supply chain and shipping professionals, whose importance became obvious to the public when global shipping disruptions emptied store shelves.
holidays.funFact: Modern shipping containers, standardized in the 1950s, helped cut the cost of shipping goods so drastically that they reshaped the entire global economy.
